description.value: The study examined fMRI cue-induced brain activation to alcohol versus neutral cues in abstinent alcohol-dependent patients and its positive association with attentional bias.

spans.text: The aim of the present study was to gain first insights into neural correlates of automatic, substance-associated attentional biases.

value: We hypothesised that the extent of initial orienting of attention towards alcohol stimuli would correlate positively with increased cue-induced brain activation in reward-associated regions in general and in the ACC, the striatum and the amygdala in particular.
